findings.title: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getSignature throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking JWT client authentication
findings.body: `AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getSignature(String sigAlgName)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")`. However, `authz-client` supports `client-jwt` authentication via `JWTClientCredentialsProvider`, which signs client assertion JWTs using `KeyWrapper` -> ` AsymmetricSignatureSignerContext` -> `ServerECDSASignatureSignerContext` / `ServerAsymmetricSignatureSignerContext` (in `keycloak-core`), or `JWKSUtils` / `JWSInput` verification, which call `CryptoIntegration.getProvider().getSignature(alg)`. When `AuthzClient` runs with `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` as the active `CryptoProvider` (i.e. without `keycloak-crypto-default` on the classpath, which is the intended use case for this provider), any signature operation going through `CryptoProvider.getSignature` will fail with `UnsupportedOperationException`.

findings.title: ECDSAAlgorithmTest uses a P-256 key for ES384 and ES512 and never verifies the re-encoded DER signature
findings.body: In `ECDSAAlgorithmTest`, `keyPair` is generated once with `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` (which defaults to a 256-bit curve) and reused for `ES256`, `ES384`, and `ES512`. Because a 256-bit key always produces ~32-byte `r` and `s` values, `testES384` and `testES512` never exercise 48-byte or 66-byte `r`/`s` values (especially the 66-byte `secp521r1` case where the leading byte is `0x00` or `0x01` and DER length exceeds 127 bytes). Furthermore, `test()` only checks that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(rsConcat))` equals `rsConcat`, without verifying `asn1Des` using `Signature.verify(asn1Des)`. If `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` produced invalid DER that `ASN1Decoder` happened to accept symmetrically, the test would still pass.

findings.title: Redundant unused ASN1Encoder allocations in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` and discard the resulting encoders before lines 119-120 perform the exact same operations inside `writeDerSeq(...)`. Those two statements are dead work and allocate unnecessary `ASN1Encoder` and `ByteArrayOutputStream` instances on every ECDSA signature conversion.
